'''Heinz-Otto Peitgen''' (born April 30, 1945 in [[Nümbrecht|Bruch]], [[Nümbrecht]] near [[Cologne]]) is a [[German people|German]] [[mathematician]] and was President of [[Jacobs University]] from January 1, 2013 to December 31, 2013. Peitgen contributed to the study of [[fractal]]s, chaos theory, and [[medical image computing]], as well as helping to introduce fractals to the broader public.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Peitgen|first1=Heinz-Otto|last2=Richter|first2=Peter H.|date=1986|title=The Beauty of Fractals|doi=10.1007/978-3-642-61717-1|isbn=978-3-642-61719-5}}</ref>

== Life ==
Peitgen studied mathematics, physics and economics from 1965 until 1971 in [[Bonn]], where he received his PhD in 1973. His doctoral dissertation was entitled “Asymptotische Fixpunktsätze und Stabilität” (English: “Asymptotic Fixed-point Theorems and Stability”).<ref>{{cite journal|last=Peitgen|first=H.O|date=July 1974|title=Asymptotic fixed-point theorems and stability|journal=Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications|volume=47|issue=1|pages=32–42|doi=10.1016/0022-247x(74)90034-1|issn=0022-247X|doi-access=free}}</ref>

After receiving his [[habilitation]] in 1977, he was awarded a professorship in mathematics at the [[University of Bremen]], where he served until 2012.{{cn|date=March 2022}} There, he was involved in establishing and developing the Institute for Dynamical Systems, where in 1982 he set up a [[computer graphics laboratory]] for mathematical experiments.{{cn|date=March 2022}} Since 1992, Peitgen has served as the director of the Center for Complex Systems and Visualization (Centrum für Complexe Systeme und Visualisierung - CeVis) at the University of Bremen.{{cn|date=March 2022}} His research specialties include mathematics, computer science and medical image computing, focusing on [[medical diagnostics]] and surgery with a particular emphasis on [[oncology]], as well as [[Neurodegeneration|neurodegenerative]]  and [[cardio-vascular diseases]].{{cn|date=March 2022}} At the beginning of his career in 1970 he contributed to computational algebraic topology.{{cn|date=March 2022}} Later in the 1980s he spearheaded fractal geometry in computer graphics, and in the early 1990s he introduced chaos theory and fractal geometry into mathematics education and spearheaded reforms in teacher training in the US.{{cn|date=March 2022}} The second half of his career was almost entirely devoted to digital applications in medicine, in particular in [[radiology]] and surgery.{{cn|date=March 2022}}

Peitgen held professorships simultaneously in Germany and the US. From 1985 until 1991, along with his professorship at the University of Bremen, he was also a professor of mathematics at the [[University of California, Santa Cruz]];{{cn|date=March 2022}} and from 1991 to 2012 he was a professor of mathematics and biomedical sciences at [[Florida Atlantic University]].{{cn|date=March 2022}} Currently,{{when|date=March 2022}} while retired from the University of Bremen, he is a professor emeritus at Florida Atlantic University.{{cn|date=March 2022}} In 1995, he founded the not-for-profit Center for Medical Image Computing, MeVis Research GmbH, in Bremen, which became a [[Fraunhofer Society]] institute at the beginning of 2009{{cn|date=March 2022}} and is now{{when|date=March 2022}} called the Fraunhofer MEVIS - Institute for Medical Image Computing.{{cn|date=March 2022}} Peitgen left the directorship of the institute in 2012, after he retired from the University of Bremen.{{cn|date=March 2022}} In 1997, Peitgen and some of his colleagues founded a commercial company, MeVis Medical Solutions AG ([[:de:MeVis Medical Solutions|de]]), MMS, which has been listed on the [[German stock market]] since 2007.{{cn|date=March 2022}} MMS is one of the world’s leading independent producers of software products for image-based medicine, particularly digital radiology.{{cn|date=March 2022}} Peitgen served as the Chairman of the Supervisory Board between 2006 and 2015.{{cn|date=March 2022}}

Peitgen has been appointed to chairs at several German and American universities and has served as a visiting professor at universities in Belgium, Brazil, Canada, the United States, Mexico and Italy.{{cn|date=March 2022}} He is the author of several award-winning books,{{cn|date=March 2022}} which were translated into German, Italian, Japanese, Chinese, Polish, and Russian and became worldwide bestsellers.{{cn|date=March 2022}} Moreover, he created a series of films that have helped to publicize fractal geometry and chaos theory around the world.{{cn|date=March 2022}} He is co-editor of several professional journals.{{cn|date=March 2022}}

In 1992, Peitgen was elected as a member of the [[European Academy of Sciences and Arts]]{{cn|date=March 2022}} and in 2008 as a member of the [[Goettingen Academy of Sciences]].{{cn|date=March 2022}} In 2015 he was elected Dean of Class IV - Natural Sciences in the European Academy of Sciences and Arts.{{cn|date=March 2022}} In 2015 he was awarded Dr.-Ing.h.c. from the Otto-von-Guericke-Universität Magdeburg for his merits in medical image computing.{{cn|date=March 2022}}

==University Leadership==
On January 1, 2013, Dr. Peitgen took over as President of [[Jacobs University]] (Former International University Bremen), Bremen, Germany.<ref>Press release of Jacobs University [http://jacobs-university.de/news-archive-2009-2015 June 8, 2012 news archive entry: "Change in leadership: Heinz-Otto Peitgen will be the next President..."] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211216155123/http://jacobs-university.de/news-archive-2009-2015 |date=December 16, 2021 }}</ref> He was successor of former President Joachim Treusch. He resigned abruptly from the post at the end of 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2014-03-25 |title=Prof. Dr. Heinz-Otto Peitgen resigns as President of Jacobs University at the end of the year {{!}} Jacobs University |url=https://www.jacobs-university.de/2013/11/prof-dr-heinz-otto-peitgen-resigns-president-jacobs-university-end-year |access-date=2022-03-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140325002346/https://www.jacobs-university.de/2013/11/prof-dr-heinz-otto-peitgen-resigns-president-jacobs-university-end-year |archive-date=2014-03-25 }}</ref>

==Awards==
* 1996: [[Verdienstorden der Bundesrepublik Deutschland|Verdienstkreuz 1. Klasse]] der Bundesrepublik Deutschland
* 1999: Karl Heinz Beckurts-Preis für Forschung und Innovation<ref>[http://www.beckurts-stiftung.de/index.php/preistraeger/  Preisträger des Karl Heinz Beckurts-Preises]</ref>  
* 2005: Werner-Körte-Medaille in Gold der Deutschen Gesellschaft für Chirurgie (DGCH)<ref>[http://www.dgch.de/deutsch/ueber-die-dgch/ehrungen/ehrungen/ Preisträger der Deutschen Gesellschaft für Chirurgie]</ref>
* 2006: Inducted as Fellow into the Charles E. Schmidt College of Science Hall of Fame at Florida Atlantic together with Benoit B. Mandelbrot <ref>{{Cite web |url=http://math.fau.edu/web/Events/Highlights/Hall%20of%20Fame%202006_files/Hall%20of%20Fame%202006.htm |title=Archived copy |access-date=2015-03-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304041313/http://math.fau.edu/web/Events/Highlights/Hall%20of%20Fame%202006_files/Hall%20of%20Fame%202006.htm |archive-date=2016-03-04 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* 2006: [[Deutscher Gründerpreis]] 2006 in der Kategorie „Visionäre“<ref>[http://www.deutscher-gruenderpreis.de/owx_1_2598_1_5_0_da64415774f275.html Deutscher Gründerpreis 2006] {{webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20130206183211/http://www.deutscher-gruenderpreis.de/owx_1_2598_1_5_0_da64415774f275.html |date=2013-02-06 }}</ref>
* 2013: Fraunhofer-Medaille<ref>[http://idw-online.de/de/news550271 Fraunhofer-Medaille für Heinz Otto Peitgen.] Pressemitteilung vom 6. September 2013 beim [[Informationsdienst Wissenschaft]] (idw-online.de)</ref>

== Selected books ==
* ''[[The Beauty of Fractals]]'', Springer, Heidelberg, 1986 (with P. H. Richter)
* ''The Science of Fractal Images'', Springer Verlag, Tokyo, Springer, New York, 1988 (with D. Saupe)
* ''Newton's Method and Dynamical Systems'', Kluwer Academic Publishers, Dordrecht, 1989
* ''Fractals for the Classroom &ndash; Part One'', Springer-Verlag, New York, and NCTM, 1991 (with H. Jürgens and D. Saupe)
* ''Fractals for the Classroom &ndash; Part Two'', Springer-Verlag, New York, and NCTM, 1992 (with H. Jürgens and D. Saupe)
* ''Fractals for the Classroom &ndash; Strategic Activities, Vol. 1'', Springer-Verlag, New York, and NCTM, 1990 (with H. Jürgens, D. Saupe, E. Maletsky, T. Perciante and L. Yunker)
* ''Fractals for the Classroom &ndash; Strategic Activities, Vol. 2'', Springer-Verlag, New York, and NCTM, 1992 (with H. Jürgens, D. Saupe, E. Maletsky, T. Perciante and L. Yunker)
* ''Fractals for the Classroom &ndash; Strategic Activities, Vol. 3'', Springer-Verlag, New York, and NCTM, 1999 (with H. Jürgens, D. Saupe, E. Maletsky, T. Perciante)
* ''Chaos and Fractals: New Frontiers of Science'', Springer-Verlag, 1992 (with H. Jürgens and D. Saupe); 2nd edition 2004, {{ISBN|0387202293}}
